---
title: "Factorization"
---

Some linguistic datasets record many measurements for each object. A vowel token may have estimates of several formant frequencies, a verb entry may have corpus counts for many subcategorization frames, and a documented phonological inventory may record whether each database segment is contrastive in that source. We can arrange such data in a matrix whose rows are objects and whose columns are measurements.

The columns may share structure. If several acoustic measurements vary together, or if sets of segments tend to recur across inventories, a smaller number of numerical patterns may approximate the matrix. Matrix factorization represents those patterns as products or sums of smaller matrices.

The factorization depends on the original representation. The [unit of analysis](../foundations/linguistic-data.qmd) determines what one row represents, while the columns determine which differences among rows can be expressed. We use **representation constraint (RC)** for this dependence: a factorization can reorganize distinctions encoded in the matrix, but it cannot decide that a token is a phoneme, that a documented inventory is a whole language, or that a corpus frame is a grammatical category. A component does not acquire a linguistic interpretation from the decomposition alone.

## From the matrix to a low-rank approximation

We begin by defining [linguistic data matrices](data-matrices.qmd), including the meanings and units of the rows and columns. [Centering and scaling](centering-and-scaling.qmd) then set the origin and relative scale of each column.

A [rank one matrix](rank-one-structure.qmd) is the outer product of one row vector and one column vector. [Singular value decomposition](singular-value-decomposition.qmd) expresses a matrix as a sum of ordered rank one terms. [Principal component analysis](principal-component-analysis.qmd) applies the decomposition to variation around the column means.

## Interpretation and reconstruction

[Scores and loadings](scores-and-loadings.qmd) distinguish coordinates for rows from directions defined over columns. [Reconstruction](reconstruction.qmd) maps retained components back to the original cells, where the difference between an observed and reconstructed value can be calculated in the units of the matrix.

[Choosing components](choosing-components.qmd) treats the retained rank as a model choice. The rank is selected on validation outcomes, and a separate test set is reserved for final evaluation. The final [VALEX--MegaAcceptability application](valex-megaacceptability.qmd) then asks whether corpus subcategorization distributions predict held-out verbs' acceptability profiles, and whether PCA compression improves that prediction.

A low reconstruction error indicates recurring numerical structure under the stated row representation, column measurements, transformations, and held-out task. It does not by itself show that a component is a psychological variable, a universal phonological dimension, or a causal process. Those interpretations require additional linguistic evidence.
